lesson.title: Comparing Groups: More, Less, and Equal
lesson.subject: math

contentBlocks.text: You can count objects and write numbers now. Today we'll use those skills to compare two groups — figuring out which group has more, which has less, or if they're equal.

Gather two small piles of objects — maybe 4 blocks and 7 buttons. Count each pile out loud. The pile with the bigger number has more; the pile with the smaller number has less. If both piles have the same number, they're equal. Try lining the two groups up side by side, one object across from another — this makes it easy to see at a glance which group has more, without even counting.
Comparing groups is something you'll use all the time in math — for sharing fairly, for measuring, and for so much more. Great practice today!

objectives: Compare two groups of objects (up to 10 in each) and correctly identify which has more, which has less, or if they're equal
Use one-to-one lining up of objects as a strategy for comparing without recounting
materialsNeeded: Two sets of small objects (e.g. blocks and buttons) for hands-on comparison
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Make two small piles of different objects and ask the child to guess which has more before counting.
2. Count each pile together out loud to check the guess.
3. Demonstrate lining the two groups up side by side, object to object, to see the difference visually.
4. Repeat with 2-3 more pairs of groups, varying which group has more/less/equal.
5. Move to the worksheet: for each pair of groups shown, write whether the first group has more, less, or is equal.
6. Close by asking the child to make their own pair of groups and describe the comparison.
differentiationTips: Struggling: stick to comparing groups of 1-5 objects before moving to larger groups
Ready for more: ask 'how many more?' or 'how many less?' as a next step beyond just identifying more/less/equal
For a child who enjoys hands-on activities, use real household objects (spoons vs. forks, socks vs. shoes) instead of the worksheet
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. More (7 is more than 4). 2. Less (3 is less than 8). 3. Equal (5 and 5). 4. More (9 is more than 6). 5. Less (2 is less than 10).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Comparing groups using more/less/equal is a core Kindergarten number-sense skill that builds directly on counting and numeral writing (this week's first two lessons), and lays the groundwork for informal addition and subtraction later this week.

worksheet.title: Comparing Groups: More, Less, and Equal

generationData.instructions: For each pair of groups, write whether the first group has MORE, LESS, or is EQUAL to the second.

rows.problem: Group A has 7 blocks. Group B has 4 blocks.
Group A has 3 stars. Group B has 8 stars.
Group A has 5 circles. Group B has 5 circles.
Group A has 9 buttons. Group B has 6 buttons.
Group A has 2 hearts. Group B has 10 hearts.
